text: objective classification scheme  assigns accessions either "core" "non-core" group based  group model best fit. target frequency patterns qualitative traits distribution  parameters quantitative traits determined first two groups:  Core Non-Core. Target proportions core group estimated base  proportions qualitative trait levels. may subjected  transformations required according "prop.adj" argument  increase rare trait representation. Target counts set scaling  total count capping actual frequency available  collection. Similarly non-core group, target proportions  determined subtracting core model's frequencies total  counts trait level entire collection. target distribution core group modeled applying  Gaussian kernel density function quantitative trait data, scaled  core size. non-core parameters set actual mean  standard deviation entire collection. Based target values, message length (\(F\)) estimated  accession models using  LEAV. accession assigned core  \(F_{core} \leq F_{non-core}\).  accessions selected  target core size, core refined ranking individuals  \(F_{core}\) values ascending order retaining top  matches.

what: Method II: Purposive selection of  accessions with highest rank  of LEAV estimates
title: Generate Core collections with Length of Encoded Attribute Values — LEAVcore_functions
text: directed selection method captures  unique dispersed accessions maximize diversity  reduce redundancy. LEAV index every accession relative entire base  collection first estimated. accessions ranked descending  order LEAV estimates.Finally core collection constituted  selecting pre-determined number top-ranked accessions according  "size" argument.

what: Method III: Stratified sampling of accessions from diversity  groups/strata computed from LEAV estimates
title: Generate Core collections with Length of Encoded Attribute Values — LEAVcore_functions
text: two-step approach  first organizes collection optimized diversity groups based  LEAV estimates followed group-wise representative sampling. also LEAV index every accession relative entire base  collection first estimated. estimates divided  \(L\) strata using Dalenius formula minimize pooled variance  (Dalenius Hodges 1959) . number entries sampled stratum determined  followed stratified selection group reach final  core size. LEAVcore3, stratification based LEAV estimates  implemented. downstream steps allocation  (allocate.basic, allocate.diversity,  allocate.distance) stratified selection  (select.random, select.diversity,  select.distance) available sister package  SampleCore.

title: Compute Information Length for Qualitative Traits — inflen.qual
code: suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(EvaluateCore))  # Get data from EvaluateCore  data("cassava_EC", package = "EvaluateCore")  # Data of 'Colour of unexpanded apical leaves' qualitative trait CUAL <- as.factor(cassava_EC$CUAL)  # Get frequencies based on sample size prop <-  prop.adj(CUAL, method = "sqrt") size.prop <- 0.2 size.count <- ceiling(size.prop * length(CUAL)) CUALfreq <- round(prop * size.count)  # Compute information length CUALinflen <- inflen.qual(x = CUAL, freq = CUALfreq, adj = TRUE)  head(CUALinflen) #>             x   inflen #> 1  Dark green 1.452784 #> 2 Light green 2.400824 #> 3  Dark green 1.452784 #> 4  Dark green 1.452784 #> 5  Dark green 1.452784 #> 6  Dark green 1.452784

title: Compute Information Length for Quantitative Traits — inflen.quant
text: quantitative trait \(d\), assumed normally distributed within subset \(t\) mean \(\mu_{d,t}\) standard deviation \(\sigma_{d,t}\) estimated . \[\mu_{d,t} = \frac{\sum x_{d,s}}{n_{d,t}}\] \[\sigma_{d,t} = \sqrt{\frac{\sum(x_{d,s} - \mu_{d,t})^2}{n_{d,t} - 1}}\] , distribution normalizing constant \(g_{d,t}\) can estimated \[g_{d,t} = \ln \left ( \frac{\sigma_{d,t}}{K \cdot \varepsilon_{d}} \right )\] \(K = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\Pi}}\), \(\varepsilon_{d}\) least count measurement descriptor \(d\). .e. \(x\) measured accuracy \(\pm\varepsilon_{d}\). probability getting measurement \(x\) distribution mean \(\mu\) variance \(\sigma\) approximately follows. \[K \cdot \frac{\varepsilon_{d}}{\sigma_{d,t}} \cdot e^{\frac{-(x_{d,s} - \mu_{d,t})^2}{2 \sigma_{d,t}^{2}}}\] Now length information code can optimally indicate possession value \(x\) trait \(d\) computed follows: \[c_{x,d,t} = g_{d,t} + \frac{(x_{d,s} - \mu_{d,t})^2}{2 \sigma_{d,t}^{2}}\]
